title: Kestrel Care Rewards Ledger Rules — Reversal of Earned Points
content:
A **Kestrel Care Rewards** earning entry can be taken back when the occasion that earned it is undone. These ledger rules govern that reversal.

## Rules

**L1 — What is reversed.** When a purchase is returned, or a prescription fill or vaccine dose that earned points is reversed, exactly the points of that earning entry are taken back.

**L2 — Once per entry.** An earning entry is reversed at most once.

**L3 — Points already converted.** Where the points of the entry have already been converted, they are taken back from the current points balance, which may go below zero until later points cover it.

**L4 — Kestrel Cash already issued.** Kestrel Cash already issued is not clawed back.

## Reading the rules

| Question | Answer under the rules |
|---|---|
| How many points come back off the membership? | Exactly the points of the earning entry being reversed — no more and no fewer. |
| Can the same earning entry be reversed a second time? | No. An earning entry is reversed at most once. |
| The balance is smaller than the points to take back. | The points are still taken back from the current balance, which may go below zero until later points cover it. |
| Kestrel Cash was issued from the converted points. | The Kestrel Cash stays; it is not clawed back. |

## Hypothetical illustration

A member's front-store purchase earned an entry of 1200 points. The balance then reached a whole block and 1000 points were converted to Kestrel Cash, leaving 200 points plus later earnings of 300, a balance of 500. The purchase is returned. Exactly 1200 points are taken back from the current balance of 500, leaving a balance of 700 below zero. The Kestrel Cash issued on the conversion stays on the membership. Points earned afterwards reduce the shortfall first: a later credit of 900 points brings the balance to 200.

A later request to reverse the same 1200-point entry again takes nothing further, because that entry has already been reversed once.
